emulator.name: QEMU 11.1.1, machine netduinoplus2 (STM32F405-class Cortex-M4F + FPU)
emulator.timing_semantics: deterministic guest instruction counts (QEMU does not emulate the DWT for this machine — probed and confirmed)
emulator.determinism: bench lines byte-identical across independent QEMU runs

hardware.board: STM32F4 Discovery (STM32F407VG, rev ?? chipid 0x413, 1 MB flash / 192 KB SRAM)
hardware.clock: HSE 8 MHz -> PLL M=8/N=336/P=2/Q=7 = 168 MHz SYSCLK, APB1 42 MHz, 5 flash WS + I/D caches (Midas constants)
hardware.timing_source: SysTick downcounter @ CPU clock (ticks = true CPU cycles) + DWT CYCCNT cross-check
hardware.clock_validation: dual-clock probe of the same 100k-iteration loop: SysTick 1200006 vs DWT 1200011 (0.0004% apart) — PLL init verified on-target
hardware.capture: ST-LINK/V2 has no VCP, so console lines are mirrored into reserved SRAM2 (0x2001C000, 'CSBL' header) and dumped via OpenOCD (firmware/stm32f4-bench/openocd-capture.cfg, Midas dump_image pattern); no USB-serial adapter needed
hardware.determinism: two full capture runs byte-identical (fixed-point math + deterministic crypto; no OS jitter)

provenance.vendoring: src/vendor/ — verbatim sources, deltas limited to import paths (std::ops->core::ops, alloc::vec), libm for std-gated f64 math (exp/ln/atan2/round), and removal of OS-entropy nonce generation
provenance.crypto_versions: pinned to core_v2/Cargo.lock: aes 0.8.4, aes-gcm 0.10.3, hkdf 0.12.4, hmac 0.12.1, sha2 0.10.9, zeroize 1.9.0 (std features off)

correctness_gates.hmac_sha256_rfc4231_case1: PASS (byte-exact KAT on target, QEMU and hardware)
correctness_gates.aes256gcm_1024B_roundtrip: PASS (ciphertext len + tag verify + decrypt match, QEMU and hardware)
correctness_gates.lambda1_sanity: 197 mnats/s @ 2000 steps IDENTICAL on desktop core_v2, QEMU, and hardware — Q32.32 bit-exactness across platforms

results.units: tck: QEMU = guest instructions; HW = true CPU cycles (SysTick @ 168 MHz, DWT-validated)

lyapunov_benettin.note: timed over a 100-step run at a distinct IC so LLVM cannot CSE it against the untimed full run; libm-heavy wrapped-coupling math dominates and benefits from the FPU + hardware divide on HW

aes256gcm_enc_1024B.note: software AES (no HW accelerator on STM32F4); includes per-call key schedule, matching core_v2 AesGcmCipher API

packet_total.composition: HKDF derive + AES-256-GCM encrypt(1024B) + HMAC-SHA256 over 1040B ct

interpretation.qemu_vs_hw: Hardware cycles run 7.3-8.0x above QEMU icount instruction counts for scalar/crypto work (flash wait states, multi-cycle loads/multiplies, per-call key schedules) — exactly the direction and rough magnitude expected for IPC << 1. The libm-heavy Lyapunov step is the outlier (1.14x): its float math uses the FPU and hardware divide, where QEMU's icount model over-counts.
interpretation.epoch_overhead: Measured on hardware: one epoch of Q32.32 RK4 key-schedule maintenance costs 82.25 G cycles = 489.6 s = 40.8% of the 1200 s epoch wall-clock. The earlier QEMU-based estimate (~65 s, 5.4%) assumed IPC=1 and is corrected by this measurement. Epoch maintenance remains schedulable (it is amortized background work, not per-packet), but it is NOT negligible and the paper must state 40.8%, not 5.4%.
interpretation.per_packet_cost: Measured on hardware: 2.51 ms per packet (421k cycles @ 168 MHz) for the full derive+encrypt+commit chain on a 1024 B payload. A 1200 s epoch with ~490 s of maintenance leaves ~118 s of headroom per packet-budget second — 195k packets/epoch of crypto budget, far above any per-satellite LEO goodput scenario in results_v3.
interpretation.feasibility_verdict: The protocol's crypto path is comfortably feasible on M4-class hardware. The honest cost is the epoch-maintenance share (~41% of the epoch in steady-state CPU time), which constrains duty-cycling but does not threaten the design.

builds.hardware: cargo build --release  # default hw: USART2 console + LEDs + PLL 168 MHz init + SRAM bench log

firmware.run_hardware: make firmware-capture  # flash + OpenOCD SRAM-dump capture + parse; ST-LINK attached (WSL: usbipd attach --wsl --busid <id>)
firmware.hw_bringup: ported from the Midas artifact (../Midas/mcu/fw/src): PLL constants, USART2 BRR (36<<4)|10, LEDs PD12..PD15, DWT enable

footprint.note: fits 1 MB flash / 112 KB linker RAM (memory.x caps RAM at 112K, reserving SRAM2 for the bench log)
